'''Caroline Finch''' AO is an Australian [[sports injury]] [[Epidemiology|epidemiologist]] and sports injury prevention researcher. Her research has been adopted and  used to directly inform safety policy by Government Departments of Sport and Health, health promotion and injury prevention agencies, and peak sports bodies both within Australia and internationally.  Her injury prevention research has been applied to falls in older people, road safety, workplace safety and injuries in children.

== Education ==
Finch graduated from [[Monash University]], [[Melbourne]] in 1983 with a BSc (Hons, 1st Class) majoring in statistics. In 1985 [[La Trobe University]] awarded her a MSc in Statistics. In 1995 she was awarded a PhD in Mathematical Statistics from Monash University for a thesis titled: ''Fasting plasma glucose distributions and their implications for the diagnostic criteria for non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus in Pacific populations''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Finch|first=Caroline Frances|title=Fasting plasma glucose distributions and their implications for the diagnostic criteria for non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus in Pacific populations|date=1994|publisher=Thesis PhD--Monash University|url=http://monash.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com/primo_library/libweb/action/display.do?tabs=detailsTab&ct=display&fn=search&doc=catau21163085770001751&indx=1&recIds=catau21163085770001751&recIdxs=0&elementId=0&renderMode=poppedOut&displayMode=full&frbrVersion=&vl(41902391UI4)=all_items&&dscnt=0&vl(1UIStartWith0)=contains&vl(1UIStartWith2)=contains&mode=Advanced&vid=MON&vl(boolOperator1)=AND&tab=default_tab&vl(drEndMonth5)=01&vl(freeText1)=&vl(drEndDay5)=01&dstmp=1521524597160&vl(drEndYear5)=1996&frbg=&vl(41902385UI0)=creator&vl(drStartMonth5)=01&vl(41902384UI2)=any&scp.scps=scope:(catelec),scope:(catau),scope:(MUA),scope:(omeka),scope:(mulo)&vl(1UIStartWith1)=contains&vl(41902386UI1)=any&srt=rank&vl(boolOperator0)=AND&Submit=%C2%A0&vl(freeText2)=&vl(boolOperator2)=AND&vl(drStartYear5)=1982&dum=true&vl(freeText0)=caroline%20finch&vl(41902387UI3)=theses&vl(drStartDay5)=01}}</ref>

At high school Finch was interested in disease prevention. As an undergraduate student she realised this interest could be combined with her strong mathematics and statistics skills which led to her career as an epidemiologist and [[Biostatistics|biostatistician]].<ref name="gettingtoknow">{{Cite web|url=https://www.monash.edu/news/articles/getting-to-know-...-caroline-finch|title=Getting to know ... Caroline Finch|website=Monash University|access-date=2018-03-20}}</ref>

== Career ==
Finch began work as a Researcher at the [[Monash University Accident Research Centre]] training in injury research from 1992 until 1997 <ref name=AOhons>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thecourier.com.au/story/5189455/australia-day-honours-2018-professor-honoured-for-work-in-sports-injury-prevention/|title=Australia Day honours 2018: professor honoured for work in sports injury prevention|last=Kirkham|first=Rochelle|date=2018-01-26|work=The Courier|access-date=2018-03-20}}</ref><ref name=gettingtoknow/> and continued from 2001 to 2003 within the Monash University, Department of Epidemiology and Preventive Medicine.<ref name=gettingtoknow/>

From 2003 to 2006 Finch was Professor and Director, NSW Injury Risk Management Research Centre, [[University of New South Wales]] and then held the position of Research Professor, School of Human Movement and Sport Sciences, [[University of Ballarat]] until 2010.

In 2010 she returned to Monash Injury Research Institute as Research Professor and [[National Health and Medical Research Council]] (NHMRC) Principal Research Fellow in the Australian Centre for Research into Injury in Sport and its Prevention (ACRISP). ACRISP is one of only nine centres worldwide recognised as International Research Centres for Prevention of Injury and Protection of Athlete Health and supported by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC).<ref name=SEMConf>{{Cite web|url=http://www.slsemconference.lk/professor-caroline-finch/|title=Professor Caroline Finch – SL SEM Conference|website=www.slsemconference.lk|access-date=2018-03-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.olympic.org/news/nine-centres-worldwide-recognised-as-ioc-research-centres-for-prevention-of-injury-and-protection-of-athlete-health|title=Nine centres worldwide recognised as IOC Research Centres for Prevention of Injury and Protection of Athlete Health|date=2016-07-21|work=International Olympic Committee|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref>

Finch became the Robert HT Smith Professor and Personal Chair at  [[Federation University Australia|Federation University]], [[Ballarat]], Australia in 2013.<ref name="conversation">{{Cite web|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/caroline-f-finch-3973|title=Caroline F Finch|website=The Conversation|access-date=2018-03-20}}</ref> In December 2017 she was appointed  Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research) at [[Edith Cowan University]], [[Perth]], [[Western Australia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ecu.edu.au/news/latest-news/2017/11/ecu-appoints-new-deputy-vice-chancellor-research|title=ECU appoints new Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research)|last=Australia|first=Edith Cowan University, Perth, Western|website=ECU |access-date=2018-03-20|date=2017-11-28}}</ref>

Finch has held positions as a sports injury prevention adviser to the Commonwealth Department of Health and Aged Care, the [[Australian Sports Commission]], [[Sports Medicine Australia]], Sport and Recreation Victoria, Department of Human Services (Victoria), the [[Victorian Health Promotion Foundation]], The [[Australian Football League]] and other national and state sports bodies.<ref name="conversation"/> She is a continuing Board Member, Sports Medicine Australia, since 2015,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sma.org.au/about-sma/board-members/|title=Board Members {{!}} Sports Medicine Australia|website=Sports Medicine Australia |access-date=2018-03-20}}</ref> a Member of the Concussion Advisory Group for [[World Rugby]], since 2014, a Member of the Victorian Government Sports Injury Prevention Taskforce from 2011 to 2013 and a Member of the  National Sports Safety Framework Committee in 1996, 1997 and  2003.<ref name=AOhons/>

Funding for Finch's research has come from the [[National Health and Medical Research Council|NHMRC]], [[Australian Research Council]], [[VicHealth]], the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the US and Canadian [[National Institutes of Health]], Australian Federal and State government departments for health and sport and from peak sports bodies including the [[International Rugby Board]], [[FIFA|Fédération Internationale de Football Association]] (FIFA), the [[Australian Football League]] and [[Cricket Australia]].<ref name=SEMConf/>

Finch has worked to improve community safety in sport and to drive significant change around children's and women's sport and in the Australian school system, to improve safety equipment and training methods in individual sports and to create a database for sports injuries. The work of Finch and her teams has led to government departments of health and peak sport bodies recognising that they have a duty of care to everyone, not just the elite athletes and that sports safety is their business as well.<ref name=AOhons/>

{{Blockquote|text="My end goal would be that any policy that has anything to do with promoting exercise or fitness or health in any context has a component that this will follow the principles of sports safety."|sign=Caroline Finch, January 2018|source=<ref name=AOhons/>}}

Finch is a Senior Associate Editor (Injury Prevention) for the [[British Journal of Sports Medicine]]<ref name="bjsm">{{Cite news|url=http://bjsm.bmj.com/pages/editorial-board/#senior|title=Editorial Board {{!}} British Journal of Sports Medicine (BJSM), Senior Associate Editors|work=British Journal of Sports Medicine (BJSM)|access-date=2018-03-22|language=en-GB}}</ref> and the Injury Prevention and Health Promotion BJSM Series<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://bjsm.bmj.com/pages/editorial-board/#iphpsenior|title=Editorial Board {{!}} British Journal of Sports Medicine (BJSM) IPHP Senior Associate Editors|work=British Journal of Sports Medicine (BJSM)|access-date=2018-03-22 }}</ref> and a member of the Editorial Boards of the international journals: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jsams.org/content/edboard|title=Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport: Editorial Board|website=www.jsams.org|access-date=2018-03-22}}</ref>  Injury Epidemiology<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://injepijournal.springeropen.com/about/editorial-board|title=Injury Epidemiology: Editorial Board|website=Injury Epidemiology|access-date=2018-03-22}}</ref> and Sports Medicine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/medicine/journal/40279?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Sports Medicine – (Editorial Board)|website=springer.com|access-date=2018-03-22}}</ref> She has published over 250 articles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Finch,+c+f|title=Finch, CF - PubMed - NCBI|last=pubmeddev|website=www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov|access-date=2018-03-22}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Finch was awarded the 2015 International Distinguished Career Award by the [[American Public Health Association]]'s (APHA) Injury Control and Emergency Health Services (ICEHS) Section. The award recognised her "outstanding dedication and leadership in injury/violence prevention and control and emergency health services internationally with contributions and achievements that have a significant and long term impact on the field".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://federation.edu.au/news?announcement_id=19366&action=view_announcement|title=News|last=Professor Caroline Finch awarded major international honour|date=2013-11-18|website=federation.edu.au|access-date=2018-03-26}}</ref>

In January 2018 Finch was made an Officer of the [[Order of Australia]] (AO), "for distinguished service to sports medicine, particularly in the area of injury prevention, as an educator, researcher and author, and to the promotion of improved health in athletes and those who exercise."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/ad2018/nls09_32z/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO.pdf|title=Australia Day 2018 Honours List: Professor Caroline Frances Finch, Officer (AO) in the General Division of the Order of Australia|date=2018-01-26|website=Governor General of the Commonwealth of Australia|access-date=2018-03-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424095834/https://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/ad2018/nls09_32z/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO.pdf|archive-date=2018-04-24|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=AOhons/>

== Projects ==
Projects Finch has been involved with include:

=== NoGAPS ===
Carried out from 2010 to 2013, NoGAPS (National Guidance for Australian football Partnerships and Safety) was a [[National Health and Medical Research Council|NHMRC]] Partnerships Project which aimed to develop, deliver, implement and evaluate new evidence-based guidelines for exercise training programs to prevent lower limb injuries in community Australian football. It aimed to identify factors that affect the application of evidence-based injury prevention interventions into practice in community sport, and to find evidence for the effectiveness of an evidence-based exercise-training program for lower limb injury prevention in community Australian football. The project involved partnerships with the Australian Football League, Victorian Health Promotion Foundation, NSW Sporting Injuries Committee, JLT Sport, a division of Jardine Lloyd Thompson Australia Pty Ltd; Department of Planning and Community Development - Sport and Recreation Victoria Division; and Sports Medicine Australia - National and Victorian Branches (SMA).<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Bekker S, Paliadelis P, Finch CF | title = The translation of sports injury prevention and safety promotion knowledge: insights from key intermediary organisations | journal =   British Journal of Sports Medicine| volume = 15 | issue = 1 | pages = 294.1–294 | date = March 2017 | pmid = 28351366 | pmc = 5371252 | doi = 10.1136/bjsports-2016-097372.26 }}</ref><ref name="gettingtoknow"/>

=== Preventing Australian Football Injuries through eXercise (PAFIX) project ===
Finch was the project leader of the 2015 PAFIX study which followed 18 community-level Australian football clubs in Western Australia and Victoria through an entire season aiming to understand and prevent knee injuries in community Australian football. The large scale  PAFIX project was unique in its use of a multi-level approach to understand the cause and prevention of knee injuries in community Australian football. Published results provide information to assist coaches and sports clubs to implement injury prevention programs.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Finch CF, Twomey DM, Fortington LV, Doyle TL, Elliott BC, Akram M, Lloyd DG | title = Preventing Australian football injuries with a targeted neuromuscular control exercise programme: comparative injury rates from a training intervention delivered in a clustered randomised controlled trial | journal = Injury Prevention | volume = 22 | issue = 2 | pages = 123–8 | date = April 2016 | pmid = 26399611 | pmc = 4819647 | doi = 10.1136/injuryprev-2015-041667 | url = }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Twomey|first1=Dara M.|last2=Doyle|first2=Tim LA|last3=Lloyd|first3=David G.|last4=Elliot|first4=Bruce C.|last5=Finch|first5=Caroline F. | name-list-style = vanc |date=2015-05-05|title=Challenges when implementing an evidence-based exercise injury prevention training program in community-level sport|url=http://bases-journal.seniortest.co.uk/index.php/JACSSES/article/view/5|journal=Journal of Applied Case Studies in Sport and Exercise Science|volume=1|issue=1}}</ref> Data was also collected during the project focusing on concussion with the aim to understand and prevent head injuries within a community Australian football setting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pafixproject.files.wordpress.com/2015/09/concussion-in-community-australian-football.pdf|title=Concussion in community Australian football: plain language statement|website=The PAFIX Project|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Fortington LV, Twomey DM, Finch CF | title = Concussion in community Australian football - epidemiological monitoring of the causes and immediate impact on play | journal = Injury Epidemiology | volume = 2 | issue = 1 | article-number = 20 | date = December 2015 | pmid = 27747752 | pmc = 5005765 | doi = 10.1186/s40621-015-0052-5 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

=== Helmets and headgear ===
Since the mid 1990s Finch has carried out studies relating to use of helmets for both pedal and motor cyclists.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Cameron MH, Vulcan AP, Finch CF, Newstead SV | title = Mandatory bicycle helmet use following a decade of helmet promotion in Victoria, Australia--an evaluation | journal = Accident Analysis and Prevention | volume = 26 | issue = 3 | pages = 325–37 | date = June 1994 | pmid = 8011045 | doi = 10.1016/0001-4575(94)90006-X }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Finch CF | title = Teenagers' attitudes towards bicycle helmets three years after the introduction of mandatory wearing | journal = Injury Prevention | volume = 2 | issue = 2 | pages = 126–30 | date = June 1996 | pmid = 9346076 | pmc = 1067676 | doi = 10.1136/ip.2.2.126 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Taylor M, Scuffham P | title = New Zealand bicycle helmet law--do the costs outweigh the benefits? | journal = Injury Prevention | volume = 8 | issue = 4 | pages = 317–20 | date = December 2002 | pmid = 12460970 | pmc = 1756574 | doi = 10.1136/ip.8.4.317 }}</ref>

In 2013 Finch jointly published results of a study of associations between helmet use and brain injuries amongst injured pedal- and motor-cyclists. The study was carried out at the [[University of New South Wales]], School of Risk and Safety Sciences under funding by an Australian Research Council (ARC) Linkage Grant: Pedal and Motor Cycle Helmet Performance Study.  The project partners were: the Commonwealth [[Department of Infrastructure and Transport]], NSW Roads and Traffic Authority (NSW RTA), [[Transport Accident Commission]] Victoria, [[NRMA]] Motoring and Services, NRMA-ACT Road Safety Trust and DVExperts International.<ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = McIntosh AS, Curtis K, Rankin T, Cox M, Pang TY, McCrory P, Finch CF |title=Associations between helmet use and brain injuries amongst injured pedal- and motor-cyclists: A case series analysis of trauma centre presentations|url=http://acrs.org.au/wp-content/uploads/ACRSjournalinsideVol24No2may13WEB.pdf|journal=Journal of the Australasian College of Road Safety|volume= 24| issue = 2, 2013|pages=11–18 }}</ref>

Finch has also been involved in research into the efficacy and methods of improvement of protective headgear in [[rugby union]], rugby league, and Australian rules football.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = McIntosh A, McCrory P, Finch CF | title = Performance enhanced headgear: a scientific approach to the development of protective headgear | journal = British Journal of Sports Medicine | volume = 38 | issue = 1 | pages = 46–9 | date = February 2004 | pmid = 14751945 | doi = 10.1136/bjsm.2002.003103 | url= | pmc = 1724753 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = McIntosh AS, McCrory P, Finch CF, Best JP, Chalmers DJ, Wolfe R | s2cid = 2503526 | title = Does padded headgear prevent head injury in rugby union football? | journal = Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise | volume = 41 | issue = 2 | pages = 306–13 | date = February 2009 | pmid = 19127196 | doi = 10.1249/MSS.0b013e3181864bee | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Finch CF, McIntosh A, McCrory P, Zazryn T |date=2003-12-01|title=A pilot study of the attitudes of Australian Rules footballers towards protective headgear|url=http://www.jsams.org/article/S1440-2440(03)80275-X/fulltext|journal=Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport |volume=6|issue=4|pages=505–511|doi=10.1016/S1440-2440(03)80275-X|pmid=14723399|issn=1440-2440|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Fall prevention in older adults ===
Finch has been involved in research around falls prevention and implementation of fall prevention strategies in older people.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Day L, Finch CF, Hill KD, Haines TP, Clemson L, Thomas M, Thompson C | title = A protocol for evidence-based targeting and evaluation of statewide strategies for preventing falls among community-dwelling older people in Victoria, Australia | journal = Injury Prevention | volume = 17 | issue = 2 | pages = e3 | date = April 2011 | pmid = 21186224 | pmc = 3064867 | doi = 10.1136/ip.2010.030775 | url = }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Finch CF, Day L, Donaldson A, Segal L, Harrison JE | title = Determining policy-relevant formats for the presentation of falls research evidence | journal = Health Policy | volume = 93 | issue = 2–3 | pages = 207–13 | date = December 2009 | pmid = 19720423 | doi = 10.1016/j.healthpol.2009.07.014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Day L, Finch CF, Harrison JE, Hoareau E, Segal L, Ullah S | title = Modelling the population-level impact of tai-chi on falls and fall-related injury among community-dwelling older people | journal = Injury Prevention | volume = 16 | issue = 5 | pages = 321–6 | date = October 2010 | pmid = 20643871 | doi = 10.1136/ip.2009.025452 | url = http://injuryprevention.bmj.com/content/16/5/321 | hdl = 2328/33233 | s2cid = 25896692 | hdl-access = free | url-access = subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Robins LM, Hill KD, Day L, Clemson L, Finch C, Haines T | title = Older Adult Perceptions of Participation in Group- and Home-Based Falls Prevention Exercise | journal = Journal of Aging and Physical Activity | volume = 24 | issue = 3 | pages = 350–62 | date = July 2016 | pmid = 26539657 | doi = 10.1123/japa.2015-0133 }}</ref>
